findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison endpoint contrasts at the observed selection nodes are strongest and most reproducible for the pair-distance shell densities: pair_kernel_1.5 (endpoint_effects:9, integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (endpoint_effects:10, z 0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0), pair_kernel_3.5 (endpoint_effects:11, z 0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_5.0 (endpoint_effects:12, z 0.319, q 3.7e-3, 0.857), while pair_kernel_7.0 is negative (endpoint_effects:13, z -0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0). The same ordering appears in the branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlations (branch_adjusted:163/164/240/241 positive; branch_adjusted:244 negative). These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a standardized coordinate observable, not an absolute geometric descriptor and not a physical interaction energy.

Shape anisotropy carries signed selection contrast: shape_yy is the most negative endpoint contrast (endpoint_effects:4, z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0), with shape_xx (endpoint_effects:3, z -0.495, q 8.1e-4) and shape_yz (endpoint_effects:8, z -0.212, q 0.035) also negative, whereas shape_xz is positive (endpoint_effects:7, z 0.185, q 0.219, not significant). The branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlations agree in sign for shape_yy (branch_adjusted:158, branch_adjusted:235). Regionally, the negative local_cyy enrichment is consistent across landmarks (e.g. regional_effects:5, 15, 75, 165, 195), so the shape signal is not confined to one region.

Landmark soft-minimum distances show mixed but reproducible signed contrasts: negative (closer) for landmark_00_softmin (endpoint_effects:14, z -0.481, q 8.1e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0) and landmark_04_softmin (endpoint_effects:26, z -0.351, q 0.014), positive for landmark_01_softmin (endpoint_effects:17, z 0.225, q 0.043), landmark_02_softmin (endpoint_effects:20, z 0.253, q 4.6e-3), landmark_03_softmin (endpoint_effects:23, z 0.360, q 0.013), landmark_05_softmin (endpoint_effects:29, z 0.396, q 2.9e-3), landmark_06_softmin (endpoint_effects:32, z 0.294, q 6.8e-4), landmark_12_softmin (endpoint_effects:50, z 0.335, q 0.012), landmark_15_softmin (endpoint_effects:59, z 0.369, q 3.7e-3), landmark_16_softmin (endpoint_effects:62, z 0.224, q 0.049) and landmark_18_softmin (endpoint_effects:68, z 0.264, q 6.0e-3). The branch-adjusted adjusted-covariance rows for landmark_18_softmin (branch_adjusted:145, branch_adjusted:299) and landmark_05_softmin (branch_adjusted:106) and landmark_15_softmin (branch_adjusted:136) agree in sign. Lower soft-min distance is a geometric proximity statement only; it does not establish a quality benefit.

Landmark occupancy shells are signed and mostly negative for the occupancy5 variant: landmark_01_occupancy5 (endpoint_effects:19, z -0.376, q 5.6e-3), landmark_02_occupancy5 (endpoint_effects:22, z -0.323, q 2.6e-3), landmark_03_occupancy5 (endpoint_effects:25, z -0.395, q 9.2e-4), landmark_05_occupancy5 (endpoint_effects:31, z -0.344, q 8.1e-4), landmark_06_occupancy5 (endpoint_effects:34, z -0.365, q 6.8e-4), landmark_12_occupancy5 (endpoint_effects:52, z -0.388, q 8.1e-3), landmark_15_occupancy5 (endpoint_effects:61, z -0.357, q 2.6e-3), landmark_18_occupancy5 (endpoint_effects:70, z -0.311, q 3.8e-3), with landmark_00_occupancy5 positive (endpoint_effects:16, z 0.208, q 0.020) and landmark_04_occupancy5 positive (endpoint_effects:28, z 0.300, q 0.033). Occupancy is a radial shell density, not an atom count and not monotone in distance.

Global centroid coordinates carry little or no reproducible signed selection contrast: endpoint_effects:0 (global_centroid_x, z -0.111, q 0.257), endpoint_effects:1 (global_centroid_y, z -0.243, q 0.014, positive batch fraction 0.214) and endpoint_effects:2 (global_centroid_z, z -0.061, q 0.481). The branch-adjusted adjusted-covariance and adjusted-correlation rows for the centroid (branch_adjusted:77-79, 231-233) are all non-significant with q >= 0.39, so the centroid is not a supported direction.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible branch-adjusted signals: joint_innovation_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:74 raw covariance q 0.038; branch_adjusted:151 adjusted covariance q 0.020; branch_adjusted:228 raw correlation q 9.3e-5; branch_adjusted:305 adjusted correlation q 2.8e-4) and joint_internal_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:76 q 0.044; branch_adjusted:153 q 0.030; branch_adjusted:230 q 1.5e-4; branch_adjusted:307 q 9.7e-4) are negative with same-sign batch fractions of 0.79-1.0, and joint_translation_RMS_A is negative but weaker (branch_adjusted:75 q 0.095; branch_adjusted:152 q 0.072; branch_adjusted:229 q 0.087; branch_adjusted:306 q 0.052). These are joint pose/shape diagnostics, not a coordinate reward and not evidence of neural-module causation.

Within-selector joint diagnostics separate coherent joint patterns from isolated marginals: innovation_native_alignment (joint_diagnostics:1, mean 0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0), teacher_innovation_contrast_alignment (joint_diagnostics:11, mean 0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0) and observed_child_score_gain (joint_diagnostics:2, mean -0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0) are the only tested associations; the contrast decomposition is dominated by the internal fraction (joint_diagnostics:14, mean 0.787) with smaller translation (joint_diagnostics:12, mean 0.132) and rotation (joint_diagnostics:13, mean 0.081) fractions. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit, not causal selection effects.

Parent-child increment contrasts are largely not significant after multiplicity adjustment: only landmark_00_softmin (increment_effects:14, q 0.046, success-failure integrated rate z -4.91), landmark_00_occupancy3 (increment_effects:15, q 0.081, z 4.28), shape_xx (increment_effects:3, q 0.095, z -3.70), shape_yy (increment_effects:4, q 0.161, z -3.85), shape_xz (increment_effects:7, q 0.207, z 3.00), pair_kernel_2.5 (increment_effects:10, q 0.208, z 3.96), pair_kernel_7.0 (increment_effects:13, q 0.208, z -3.14), landmark_03_occupancy5 (increment_effects:25, q 0.161, z -3.02) and landmark_16_occupancy3 (increment_effects:63, q 0.222, z -1.75) reach q < 0.25, and none reach q < 0.04. The increment contrasts therefore do not by themselves establish a within-path change.

Turnover accounting separates population-contrast change from cohort composition: for landmark_00_soft_mass the edge rate is positive (turnover:1, z 4.55, q 0.142) while the turnover residual is negative (turnover:2, z -4.36, q 0.142), and for landmark_00_local_cxx the edge rate is negative (turnover:13, z -4.34, q 0.055) while the residual is positive (turnover:14, z 4.29, q 0.038). Large positive residuals also appear for landmark_00_local_cyy (turnover:17, z 5.05, q 0.033), landmark_01_local_cyy (turnover:47, z 6.40, q 0.014), landmark_04_local_cxx (turnover:134, z 5.67, q 0.012), landmark_07_local_cyy (turnover:227, z 5.63, q 0.019), landmark_08_local_cxx (turnover:254, z 5.54, q 0.012), landmark_16_local_cyy (turnover:497, z 6.37, q 0.012), landmark_17_local_cxx (turnover:524, z 5.24, q 0.012) and landmark_19_local_cxx (turnover:584, z 5.30, q 0.012). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.

Descendant survival credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity: positive survival enrichment appears for landmark_00_soft_mass (survival_effects:0, z 0.365, q 0.120), landmark_07_soft_mass (survival_effects:70, z 0.220, q 0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass (survival_effects:100, z 0.234, q 0.302) and landmark_18_local_czz (survival_effects:186, z 0.217, q 0.302), while negative survival enrichment appears for landmark_04_local_czz (survival_effects:46, z 0.266, q 0.302), landmark_05_local_czz (survival_effects:56, z -0.419, q 0.120), landmark_07_local_cyy (survival_effects:75, z -0.299, q 0.219), landmark_09_local_czz (survival_effects:96, z -0.390, q 0.120), landmark_14_local_czz (survival_effects:146, z -0.308, q 0.120), landmark_15_local_czz (survival_effects:156, z -0.399, q 0.155), landmark_16_local_cyy (survival_effects:165, z -0.317, q 0.219) and landmark_19_local_cyy (survival_effects:195, z -0.294, q 0.302). Because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, these last-record credits cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

The supplied continuous trends are observed-node linear fits over the observed window only, with extrapolation disallowed, and the curve-fidelity audit rejects polynomial acceptance for the audited features (polynomial_accepted false throughout) with relative node RMSE 0.29-0.99 and multiple strong sign conflicts (e.g. continuous:1 has 9 strong sign conflicts, continuous:7 has 14). The information audit further reports that the compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS is 0.081 A (CI 0.070-0.092) and the chosen-teacher score correlation is 0.102 (CI 0.065-0.140), with the explicit limitation that these are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian. Curve fitting therefore does not establish a causal benefit or a coordinate gradient.

Scope and clock constraints: the observed score times and learning window are [0.0, 0.5] with curve support [0.0, 0.49], the label semantics are recorded affinities removed with an equal score prior, and decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable. The lineage support table covers 14 complete-survival batches with 700 total batch nodes, 349 nodes having fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 fewer than 6, and terminal metadata at terminal_index 99 (score time 0.99, state time 1.0) with one future resampling node per batch. The objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; temperatures are immutable fixed parameters (mixture_temperature 0.5, teacher_endpoint_temperature_A2 4.0) and no temperature edit is proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Hypothesis: a coordinate intervention that increases the density of pair distances in the 1.5-5.0 A shells while decreasing the 7.0 A shell would move the endpoint pointcloud along the most reproducible signed selection contrast. Observable: pair_kernel_1.5/2.5/3.5/5.0/7.0 endpoint contrasts. Intended response: positive integrated z for the 1.5-5.0 shells and negative for 7.0. Target origin: observed selection nodes over the complete observed window. Scale: pair-distance shells of 1.5-7.0 A with sigma 0.75 A. Discriminating failure: if the 1.5-5.0 shells do not remain positive across independent batches, or if the 7.0 A shell does not remain negative, the direction is not supported. This is a measurable contrast target, not a physical interaction energy.

Hypothesis: reducing shape_yy (and to a lesser extent shape_xx and shape_yz) while leaving shape_xz free would follow the signed shape contrast. Observable: shape_yy, shape_xx, shape_yz, shape_xz endpoint contrasts. Intended response: more negative shape_yy and shape_xx, more negative shape_yz, shape_xz unconstrained. Target origin: observed selection nodes. Scale: shape covariance entries in A^2. Discriminating failure: a sign reversal of shape_yy in the branch-adjusted adjusted correlation or a loss of the negative local_cyy regional pattern would weaken the direction. The shape entries are coordinate covariance descriptors, not an inferred chemical mechanism.

Hypothesis: landmark soft-minimum distances are region-specific rather than globally uniform, with landmark_00 and landmark_04 favoring closer approach and landmarks 01, 02, 03, 05, 06, 12, 15, 16 and 18 favoring greater separation. Observable: landmark_XX_softmin endpoint contrasts. Intended response: negative for landmark_00/04, positive for the listed others. Target origin: observed selection nodes. Scale: soft-min distance in A with T = 0.5 A. Discriminating failure: if the landmark_18_softmin sign does not reproduce in the branch-adjusted adjusted covariance, or if the landmark_00_softmin sign flips, the region-specific claim is not supported. Lower soft-min distance is geometric proximity only.

Hypothesis: the large positive turnover residuals for local_cxx and local_cyy at several landmarks reflect changing cohort composition and score reclassification rather than within-path coordinate change, because the corresponding parent-child increment contrasts are mostly not significant after multiplicity adjustment. Observable: turnover_residual_rate versus increment success-failure integrated rate. Intended response: large residual with small increment contrast. Target origin: whole-window rate accounting. Scale: per-window rate z-scores. Discriminating failure: a significant increment contrast in the same feature would indicate within-path change instead. The residual is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect.

Hypothesis: the reproducible joint-motion signal is dominated by internal deformation rather than translation or rotation, since the contrast internal fraction is 0.787 versus 0.132 translation and 0.081 rotation, and joint_internal_RMS_A and joint_innovation_RMS_A are the most reproducible branch-adjusted negatives. Observable: joint_internal_RMS_A, joint_innovation_RMS_A, joint_translation_RMS_A. Intended response: negative for internal and innovation, weaker for translation. Target origin: joint pose/shape diagnostics. Scale: RMS in A. Discriminating failure: if the translation fraction dominates in an independent batch or the internal RMS sign flips, the coupling claim is not supported. These are joint diagnostics, not a coordinate reward.

Hypothesis: recorded descendant survival credit and endpoint selection contrast disagree in direction for several features (for example positive survival enrichment for landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_07_soft_mass versus negative survival enrichment for landmark_05_local_czz, landmark_07_local_cyy, landmark_09_local_czz, landmark_14_local_czz, landmark_15_local_czz, landmark_16_local_cyy and landmark_19_local_cyy), and this disagreement should affect direction priorities. Observable: survival_enrichment_z versus endpoint integrated z. Intended response: direction priority follows the endpoint contrast where the two disagree. Target origin: recorded joint-head survival credit. Scale: whole-window enrichment z. Discriminating failure: without decoded terminal labels the comparison cannot be resolved, so last-record credit must not be presented as final affinity benefit. This comparison is reported as unavailable.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling, and is an accounting diagnostic rather than a causal selection effect or atom velocity.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis is available and extrapolation is disallowed.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects are retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
Temperatures are immutable fixed parameters and no temperature edit is proposed.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so the cited pair-kernel and moment effects are diagnostic evidence only.
